newsitem.title: USA: Salomon Inc. has higher quarter, year earnings.
newsitem.headline: Salomon Inc. has higher quarter, year earnings.

text.p: Salomon Inc., the diversified investment and commodity trading house, Tuesday reported higher fourth-quarter and full-year earnings, citing particular strength in its Salomon Bros. and Phibro units.

"Strong performances at Salomon Bros. and Phibro produced fourth-quarter results that are a suitable conclusion to a very successful year," said Robert E. Denham, chairman and chief excecutive officer.
Wall Street reacted favourably to one of its own, sending Salomon's stock up $2.375 to $51.50 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
For the fourth quarter, Salomon Inc. earned $228 million, or $1.98 a share, on revenues of $2.21 billion. A year earlier it earned $168 million, or $1.42 a share, on revenues of $2.37 billion.
For the year, Salomon earned $907 million, or $7.88 a share, on revenues of $9.0 billion. In 1995, Salomon had earnings of $457 million, or $3.64 a share, on revenues of $8.9 billion.
At Salomon Bros., the company's global investment banking and securities business, pretax earnings of $1.36 billion for the year nearly doubled the $704 million earned in 1995.

Global investment banking revenues for the year were $853 million, up 81 percent over the $472 million in 1995. Fixed income sales and trading net revenues were $2.6 billion, up from $1.6 billion a year earlier.

Equity sales and trading revenues were $389 million, down from $828 million in 1995. Salomon said the decrease reflected losses on the company's long-term proprietary equity and lower revenues from customer sales and trading.
Phibro, the company's commodity trading business, reported pretax earnings for the year of $192 million, more than double the $85 million earned in 1995.

Basis Petroleum, its oil refining and marketing business, had a pretax loss of $123 million for the year, compared with a pretax loss of $91 million in 1995. Basis' 1996 results were affected by costs associated with a planned reconfiguration of its refining system.
